paths.description: Homepage/entry template: navigation, promotions, preferences, security, performance and crawler baseline.
Search/listing archetype for “phone”: discovery, filters, result cards and direct add-to-cart affordances.
Deals/listing archetype representing promotional category browsing.
Product-detail archetype: price, seller, fulfilment, returns and purchase CTAs.
Error/recovery surface reached from a direct sign-in route.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains the same bright white/orange composition as the default screenshot; no surface retint is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border and image treatments.

findings.summary: Transient navigation UI is custom rather than semantic.
findings.evidence: The modern-feature probe found 0 popover, 0 dialog and 0 details elements despite account, language, category and carousel flyouts in the storefront.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient flyouts to popover and modal flows to dialog with declarative light-dismiss and focus handling.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome crowds the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot devotes the first viewport to two navigation rows, a large rotating promotion and eight competing merchandise cards before a coherent product task begins.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneous promotional modules and preserve a clearer primary shopping hierarchy.

findings.summary: Pages ship a desktop layout to narrow screens.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, the page has no viewport meta and reports a 1000 CSS-pixel layout with 640px overflow; the screenshot clips the search bar, hero and cards. Search, deals and product templates also report no viewport meta and a 1000px layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a width=device-width viewport meta and replace the 1000px minimum layout with intrinsic, fluid responsive templates.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small and some keyboard focus states are absent.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe found 8x4px flyout buttons and 15–20px-high links; multiple shortcut/search controls computed no outline or box shadow on focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Use at least 24x24 CSS-pixel targets (prefer 44x44 for primary touch actions) and a consistent visible :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.8s and LCP 17.2s with a performance score of 0.58.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP image, reduce critical resource chains and defer non-critical work and below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers a heavy, poorly prioritised resource set.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 244 requests and 4.09MB transferred, including 184 images/3.07MB and at least eight parser-inserted high-priority stylesheet/script candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Limit initial hero variants, lazy-load below-fold imagery, consolidate critical CSS, and set explicit fetch priority only on the true LCP resource.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and CSS ship on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 496KiB unused JavaScript and 139KiB unused CSS; the WAF challenge alone contributed about 328KiB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by surface, conditionally load optional modules and remove duplicated/legacy CSS and JS.

findings.summary: ARIA semantics are invalid on prominent controls.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found two disallowed ARIA attributes, an invalid role="close", and a cart accessible-name/content mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Use valid roles and state attributes, and ensure each control’s visible label is included in its accessible name.

findings.summary: The home page lacks a top-level heading and focus visibility is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found no h1. Several keyboard shortcut and search elements had no visible outline or box shadow when programmatically focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a meaningful h1 for the page purpose and standardise visible focus indication across every interactive element.

findings.summary: Missing viewport configuration prevents usable mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: All four commerce templates inspected lacked viewport meta and rendered a scaled 1000px desktop canvas at 360px; controls and text are miniaturised rather than reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scalable viewport and responsive layout, then test reflow at 320 CSS px and browser zoom up to 400%.

findings.summary: The page logs a JavaScript module error during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a console.error for “Late loading module @m/mash” from an Amazon script.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the late module dependency/order and keep production console error-free.

findings.summary: Image markup is broadly unsized and legacy-format heavy.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 79/100 images without dimensions, 92 without srcset, 99 legacy-format images, 85 below-fold images without lazy loading and 22 missing alt; Lighthouse also found an incorrect aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit dimensions/aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats and lazy loading, and supply meaningful or empty alt as appropriate.

findings.summary: Deprecated browser API use and inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported deprecated Shared Storage API usage, cookie-related inspector issues and a best-practices score of 0.50.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and resolve DevTools inspector issues before they become compatibility failures.

findings.summary: Crawler and mobile fundamentals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The page has no viewport meta; the probe found five javascript: links and Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add viewport metadata and replace JavaScript pseudo-links with buttons or real crawlable href destinations.

findings.summary: The declared sitemap endpoint is missing.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is reachable and the home page has a canonical URL, but /sitemap.xml returned a styled 404 document rather than a sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap indexes for public localized/category/product URLs and reference them from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Entity/share metadata is incomplete on the sampled entry page.
findings.evidence: The home metadata probe found no JSON-LD and an empty twitter:card; the page has og:description but no demonstrated complete social card.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and Product structured data where applicable, plus complete Open Graph and Twitter card metadata.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but the headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence found five cookies with insecure attributes, including session-id without HttpOnly and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection and explicit privacy policies; harden session-like cookies with Secure, HttpOnly and appropriate SameSite.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated homepage initiates extensive advertising/cookie-sync activity.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 237 of 244 requests and 3.88MB to non-main origins. Lighthouse observed 25 third-party cookies and many cookie-sync endpoints with empty GDPR consent parameters.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise third-party collection, gate non-essential advertising sync behind valid consent, batch telemetry and document purpose/retention.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policy coverage is absent.
findings.evidence: The response has no HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; Lighthouse also surfaced third-party cookie inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit least-privilege browser policies and move third-party integrations toward partitioned/privacy-preserving storage.

findings.summary: Core public content is almost absent without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched 2,007 bytes of raw HTML with only 1% rendered-word coverage; title and meta description were absent and the result was classified as a JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or stream meaningful navigation, headings, listings and product content, then enhance interactions with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The app-like commerce experience exposes no install/offline surface.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found no web app manifest. The site is an app-like repeat-use commerce service, but no offline fallback or registered installation metadata was evidenced.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and a narrowly scoped service worker with an honest offline/retry fallback for browsed content and cart state.

findings.summary: Image delivery is disproportionately wasteful.
findings.evidence: Images account for 3.07MB of the 4.09MB transfer; 99/100 sampled images use legacy formats, 92 lack srcset and 85 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive sources and intrinsic dimensions, and lazy-load non-critical assets.

findings.summary: Initial loading performs substantial work unrelated to immediate content.
findings.evidence: The load makes 244 requests, 237 to non-main origins; Lighthouse estimates 496KiB unused JS and records extensive advertising cookie synchronisation.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load optional/ad modules after consent and intent, and eliminate background fetches that provide no current-session value.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: Non-main origins transfer 3.88MB and images transfer 3.07MB; the visible first viewport does not justify loading 184 images and 21 fonts up front.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level byte/request budgets, defer third parties and below-fold media, and subset/preload only required fonts.

findings.summary: Repeated carousel interaction leaves measurable retained growth.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary was 25.26MB/413,147 nodes; after ten carousel-next interactions it was 28.08MB/428,763 nodes, growth of 2.82MB and 15,616 nodes. Separate browser sessions lower confidence that all growth is a leak, but the retained delta warrants investigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one controlled session, identify retained paths, and release obsolete carousel nodes/listeners/timers.

findings.summary: The initial DOM/heap footprint is large for a landing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline summary contains 413,147 heap nodes and 25.26MB self size before meaningful interaction, alongside 100 images and a long promotional feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or defer below-fold modules, reduce duplicated markup and bound caches to keep the landing-page footprint proportionate.
